So, I said to my nephew, "I really like it. But, who the f plays a game like this til they beat it 8 times?"

I think I'm up to 5 or 6 times.

Don't take my "hours played" seriously. I used to leave it running in the background. But I've gotta be 80 hours in at least.

Very underrated game. I have a love of platformers and roguelikes, so this was a wonderful combination of the two (Spelunky 2 is one of my favorite games as well, go figure). Gives immense replayability- I 100%'d it but could've kept going for quite a while more.

The bad part of the game to me was the beginning, where you are learning all the bosses and biomes for the first time. To me, this process is usually the most fun part of a roguelike, but I found myself frustrated in this game and bounced off it for a while. Once you get that first clear under your belt, the game feels like it really opens up in the NG+ playthroughs.

This is an easy contender for my favorite game ever; what a trip it's been from EA to NG+100.

What appeals to me the most apart from the incredibly fluid combat system is the progression that actively rewards you varying your playstyle while leaving enough breathing room to pursue the one you enjoy the most. Fantastic graphics, superb challenge, great music, fun secrets, nice characters, and the most addictive gameplay loop I've ever experienced to this day. Also works phenomenally well on the Deck, even has a native Linux port.

Something else to note is that the early access experience was stellar. Cellar Door Games delivered on time, every time, consistently high quality content and updates all the while having paid close attention to what feedback the community gave. We even got detailed patch notes and reasoning behind many of the changes along the way.

I can not overstate enough
Way, waaaaaay better then Hollow Knight: Silksong, yet not nearly as richly rewarded and acclaimed... Life is truly not fair. This game is amazing, buy it.

Overall a huge improvement on the original. The new classes / weapons add a lot to the variety of a playthrough and the gold increase of negative traits makes them an actually interesting decision to make. Game has a lot of charm with the small snippets of lore you get over the game, and although I prefer the artstyle of the original it feels a lot smoother to play. The heirloom system is a really good change too, I much prefer it over the previous Rune system due to it's limitations.

The enchantress is really hot too. need that.
This is seriously one of the best games ever made, the gamplay is very satisfying, the loop is addictive and the lore is very fun to uncover.

No i-frame doge and enemies are programmed to rush to the player while also spamming projectiles that go through walls and enemies that do really fast charge attacks from off screen. To top it off they also have made half their challenges, fight X amount of enemies while avoiding X hazards and don't take any damage. 

Interesting ideas but unfortunatly none of them qualify as progression. You very quickly realize the games difficulty scaling far outpaces the power they make available to the player as "progression." So fail or succeed the game gets more difficult, making the former too punishing. 

Its adequate for the price but don't see myself playing more than 10hours max. I don't think is for me 6/10.
Amazing casual game, everything is well polished, graphics are nice, didnt find any bugs for my 237 hours of playing

extremely well crafted.  good meta progression, excellent boss design, varied enemy design and colorfully different biomes.  the end game repeats drags on but they give you an option to shortcut if you choose.

I loved the first game and this one is an improvement in almost every way. Classes are more interesting, more content in the castle, more story as well. Very well done, and one of my favorite games of all time.

I played this game a few years ago, and I really really enjoyed it.

An outstanding 2D platformer with really, really TIGHT movement and a wide variety of gameplay styles. 15 classes and 30 weapons overall - EACH of them offers a different attack style, from a basic sword swing in front of character, or narrow lunges but in 4 directions (like in Hollow Knight), to AOE attacks, boomerang attacks, and even jumping on static projectiles you place beforehand. Rogue Legacy 2 manages to combine a lot of mechanics from different platformers and blend them into one thing, where you can CHOOSE what you want to play and master. Worth mentioning, you won't be forced to play everyone or lock in to a single character/weapon, but this game does a great job of encouraging you to conquer different playstyles, since you gain bonuses for leveling them up and rare valuable traits sometimes roll on characters you don't normally play, so...

Overview: This game is a top-tier contender for rogue-likes. Hundreds of ways to customize your builds, ways for runs to go, and even various accessibility options make this game the right choice for anyone wanting to kill some time

- Story: Not gonna lie, completely SPRINTED through the story. Not really sure what exactly is going on, other than there are some religious references going on. I do like how there is a true ending for this game, which helps players continue playing, even after the first successful playthrough.

- Gameplay: Standard rogue-like, but I'd say A LOT more forgiving than most. This game is all about gathering resources to upgrade your character and armor, then keep going until you eventually succeed. There are also accessibility options so those with disabilities can still enjoy the game. If you look up what exactly these options are, then hopefully they work

Ridiculously faithful to the previous instalment. To the point where I now genuinely feel like I'm playing a decked-out & fully flushed modded version of the 1st Rogue Legacy. I had to go look at screenshots of the first game to convince myself that this isn't how that game always looked.

Anyway, a statue called me smelly and then proceeded to give me a very fun to solve challenge. This is really good and lining up to be even better. A deserved upvote for this game!

This is another installment in one of the greatest rouge-like games I've every played - its for sure my favorite. I'm not particularly good at these types of games, but it rewards persistance and there is a great amount of variety and a ton of content that never feels stale.

The game is to grindy.  I love that the play session is just 10-15 minuts. but then you don't se much progression. and starting from scratch with all knowledges doesn't improve much. 
Inflation on the purchases looks like just a patch or artificial obstacle, to prevent fast progression. This game doesn't deserve 60 or 100 hours to complete.
Rogue Legacy is on of my favorite roguelikes and this is significantly better at everything the first one does, rogue legacy but everything is 2x as good

What a fantastic game. Blending metroidvania with a roguelike in a briliant execution.

The first one was really good, but this one is pushed to perfection.
Huge variety and every bit of it is fun.

I love this game.

It's easy to play in short spurts, which is nice when you are busy and only have a little time to play here and there. That's really important for me - to be able to pop in and out of a game quickly. I like arcade and rogue lite games because you can do that. 

I also enjoy the fact that you can scale the difficulty through the settings by lowering enemy health, damage, etc. I think purists will hate that because it makes getting the achievements and things much easier, but for those of us who are casual gamers, it allows us to experience the game to its fullest. I played the first game and felt like it was too hard at the end. This one is just right for me. 

If I have a criticism, it can feel grindy at times - but I fixed that by changing the difficulty which allowed me to make steady progress. 

All in all, this is a great game.

an amazing sequel(prequel) to my most favorite roguelite game of all time, i love everything about this game, especially the story and the ost :p
also the game and the devs are woke (based)

Such an amazing little game. Goes to show that these big companies that spend 200 million for live service slop, have lost their way. Meanwhile these indie devs sell more than those big Sony, M$, and Nintendon'ts games.

It didn't quite live up to my expectations because it's very similar to the first game, but with some graphic improvements.
The level layout becomes repetitive / predictive and there was a point where I was forced to end a run prematurely because I fell out of the world.
The constant pizza jokes feel out of place. I'm inclined to believe they were added later in development, especially since the Vegan trait hurts you when you touch pizza despite saying it only hurts you if you touch meat.
The game artificially extends the time it takes to gain enough levels and beat it. Thus making this game 3 times longer then the first one, but not adding enough content / variety to justify the increase in length.
Though it still gets a good review because it was good enough for me to play through to the end.
It takes the foundation of the first one and improves on basically all aspects? Looks better, controls better, has more interesting builds, challenges and all that. Quite neat.
I was surprised that this adds a lot of new bonus stuff over the first game.  Worth giving a shot.

Its not a bad game, but it has two really bad problems

1- All the upgrades that give new classes and facilities are too frontloaded meaning that you unlock them all within an hour then spend the rest of your playtime unlocking meaningless crap like +1 armor or +10 health. Theres nothing interesting to save up for

2- The game wants to challenge you with platforming as much as it does with combat. The problem is the platforming is so bad with the controls and giant character size that it just gets annoying

The game is good, the directional bug is bad. If I point my character left or right I expect the character to aim that way. This bug was present in the original game too. You think they would have fixed it by now..

I wanted to add a little more info. This particular bug is something that happens in both games with controllers. Cellar Door games needs to fix this bug with their controller support. If you do a quick turn around with the analog stick the character will either backslide or turns back to original direction. It's very frustrating, especially when dying constantly due to this bug.

Rogue Legacy 2, a rogue like obviously, that fell pretty flat on its face for me.

The moment to moment gameplay and presentation is fine. What really killed this one for me is the meta progression. I could go on about the ins and outs of how the meta progression is designed very purposefully to make you try new things, learn how weapons/classes work together and so on and so forth... but all that fell apart for me when I had to start grinding. You need to get some rather large sums of money to unlock small percent upgrades to health and damage. It is not fun grinding for these. And if you want these upgrades to be meaningful you'll need to get several of them, aka a LOT of grinding. You can attempt to just push forward through to the main goals, but it will get harder and harder until those upgrades become necessary. The devs tried to address this issue by adding a gold bonus to next

Eh.... It's a more polished version of Rogue Legacy, but more grindy and repetitive due to poorly designed upgrade scaling. It has two more biomes than the original game, but those two are very linear and they wear out their welcome quickly. The entire sidescrolling roguelite subgenre is aging badly. There are three more I plan to play in the future but after that I am DONE with this subgenre for good. I recommend playing summum aeterna instead of this if you really want a sidescrolling roguelite, its less grindy and even more fluid.

I may change this review at a later date, but based on my first few hours, I can't really say I recommend the game.

Don't get me wrong, there's a lot going for the game, but for me personally, it didn't hook me the same as RL1, I think primarily because of scope-creep.

This game is cute and has some unique mechanics, but it's hampered by the absolute SLOG that is the progression. I understand that you're supposed to go through lots of characters, but on a lot of runs it feels like nothing gets done and that my time and currency were wasted. If the gameplay were better, this might be OK, but it's really just super basic metroidvania combat (jump, attack, airdash, pogo) and doesn't feel as smooth as something like Silksong or even OG Hollow Knight. I quickly stopped playing after I realized that the combat wasn't going to get much deeper.

The Legacy system is a neat idea, but I was expecting something like Mewgenics that allowed you to nudge your characters into a niche or something, but nope! No alternate starting weapons, starting skills, or ways to increase the amount of variety. You just get 3 choices that give you slightly more gold when they hav

The bones of the game are as good as the first one, maybe even better.
The second area ruined the game for me.
I wanted to love it as much as the first, but I couldn't.
Maybe it's a skill issue but I honestly thing the design is fundamentally flawed.

Like Dead Cells, but much worse.

Three things and it might be personal taste or just bad design. I'll let you decide.

1. The character is ginormous and looks clumsy when they move and feels clumsy when they play.
2. Enemies shoot you from offscreen. A lot. Which that's never good game design imo.
3. This is much more of a parkour game than something like Dead Cells. It has similar opponents and similar controls and similar movement, but it comes at you with the platforming as hard as it comes at you with the opponents and when you combine this with issue number 1 it just doesn't work well.

I wouldn't recommend it at any price because there are other options which are much better.
It is ultra grindy cookie clicker where you must die infinite times to upgrade your character. I don't like it.

I really wanted to like this as a huge fan of the first game, but every second of this game is agony. In as nice a way as I can put it: it feels like a fan project more than anything. Like someone's outside perspective on the game and what it should be, instead of ANYTHING the original game had going for it. gg go next I guess.

No, getting hit constantly by offscreen enemies should not be the norm.
No, putting the player in a closet with traps and a projectile spamming boss that floats at you is not okay.
No, adding a second boss to the closet does not make it better.
No, a player should not die in three hits despite farming the whole map every run.
No, making five of the eight bosses randomly overlay several projectile attacks at a time is not game design. 
No, adding more sets of projectiles to the boss won't fix that.
No, the boss minions that home in on the player should not be invincible for 30 seconds during his other attacks.
No, the correct response to overwhelming negative feedback on a new mode isn't to suggest players enable cheats for it.

No, the devs shouldn't be proud of any of this.
No, absolutely not.

Rogue Legacy 2 is an okay game but the massive grind of the meta progression really detracts from the experience and is not satisfying at all (minor and lame % increases/decreases or stat changes for huge sums of currency). The platforming and hitbox damage can also be quite annoying due to your character's size. Overall this gets a "meh" from me. If you really like to grind you might enjoy this game but I enabled house rules to finish the last area as I couldn't be bothered to grind as much as I would need to. Kind of a bummer since the first game had the same issue.

I think that the premise of the game is so interesting, with every run being a new person, but it's ruined by the people in the "lobby" staying the same and even the blacksmith saying that every new character you play is just the same person, breaking the 4th wall etc. it ruins the immersion and just treats the premise as unimportant.
I actually quite like this game, but whoever added the boogie board scar is evil. It's aids and controls like ♥♥♥♥ compared to the regular game.

Too much grind, game controls feel unresponsive, bosses start to spam the whole arena with aoe skills, story is non existent so if you don't enjoy grinding game is not for you because it cannot provide anything beside grinding

edit: forgot to mention that meta progression is make the whole run with eye bleeding filter to get +1 to health, so even grind isn't fun as it is pointless

on a plus side game has a house rules menu that makes game easier but after playing with it i don't see the point, after all by removing awful gameplay you are removing 90% of the game so if might as well just not play the game instead of running thru it with some silly 50% damage resistance to read notes about [spoiler] bosses going insane in the past [/spoiler]

I bought this game and after getting through the tutorial the games atmosphere was immediately violated with Christmas presents all over the place and Christmas hats on every enemy. I tried to change my computers date but then Steam won't let the game turn on because it breaks the secure connection. Why would I want to play a medieval fantasy game with Christmas hat jpegs plastered on every enemy, when I can play a game that cares about art direction and atmosphere.
Honestly just really grindy and boring

Strangely, I had almost the exact same experience with Rogue Legacy 2 as I did with the first game.
I didn’t really enjoy it. Which raises the question of why I decided to play the sequel in the first place. This is a genuine question, as I have no idea, apart from the fact that I must have misremembered how I felt about the first one until I finished the second.

I think I can safely say: if you liked the first one, you’ll like this one. 
If you didn’t like the first one... then don’t play the second (which should be obvious, but then again, you might be like me).
for the precision that is required the controls and overall handling suck. enemies annoy me rather than challenge me. for the first hour it was addicting but I see no value in continuing
Gets really old in 7 runs, and I really enjoy roguelikes.

Felt really annoyed playing this.  I think a lot of my problems would be fixed with a smaller map, like you're limited in the amount of upgrades you can carry without reducing max health which seems to be the game's way of telling you to only do 1-2 zones per run, you can't refight bosses because they just stay dead (until you do a new save or ng+ apparently) which again seems to be the game telling you only do newest zone, the game locks zones off by upgrades so you can't try accessing high level areas early on for better rewards if you feel confident, wayyyy too much grinding for gold for upgrades, the difficulty per zone seems to be 90% determined by your class (wide open area play archer and you're untouchable, but take them in a zone with high enemy density and you're done for).  It's also weird, they added changing difficulty for accessibility like lower enemy damage, perma flying,
I played all of this game in a dissasociative haze. I barely remember it besides not having the best of times. Kinda a middle of the road Castlevania/Roguelike.
